title: Mobile & Compatibility Renderer Max Lights does not take Light3D Distance Fade into account
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot v4.6.1.stable (14d19694e)

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable (14d19694e) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.23033.1002) - AMD Ryzen 5 5500 (12 threads) - 15.89 GiB memory

### Issue description

My game uses the Mobile renderer (also tested on Compatibility. Forward+ it is not a noticeable issue). I have a large map which requires multiple light sources during the night. I enable distance fade on the lights for performance & distances can be far apart so they may all not be needed, however the lights reach the max cap despite not all of them being faded in/visible. Setting the node visibility to false fixes this.

I suppose there can be work arounds for this like a script on each light node to track distance to camera & change the node visibility instead but that seems like it defeats the purpose of the distance fade feature?

### Steps to reproduce

- Have over 8 OmniLight3Ds or SpotLight3Ds shining on the same mesh (like a large plane).
- Only 8 will be visible on the mesh.
- Enabling distance fade to any distance, will not affect this culling.
- Disabling an active light visibility (even if its faded out) will make another light visible on the mesh.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[maxlightMRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26368739/maxlightMRP.zip)

You should have a scene with a bunch of OmniLight3Ds with distance fade settings, shining onto a plane mesh. Moving the camera around you should only see max 8 active, disabling the visible ones will make another visible, regardless of distance.
